# Count quantization effect

Source: paper_materials/quantization.log

All cases use **W3 + P2**. Columns are quantization sizes. Card rows are the resulting count weights. The performance rows use the 1:10 spread edge and **Kelly growth at multiplier 1 (@1)**; empirical optimal-Kelly values are intentionally excluded.

In a performance cell, **Δ** is the signed percentage change from that case's exact q=0 result. Spread change is measured relative to the absolute baseline edge, so it remains intuitive when the baseline edge is negative. Kelly change is measured on excess growth, growth − 1. A negative Δ is degradation; a positive Δ is improvement.
